errors.english: Furthermore, if a doubt were to arise here, consider the case of a (mya ngan) mirage in a desert or wilderness where even a small object appears large.
errors.why: The Tibetan says that even if that doubt could arise in the mantra case, there is no such doubt in the case of deserts where small things appear large; the English drops the key 'there is no doubt' and also glosses mya ngam (desert) as 'mirage'.

fix.find: Furthermore, if a doubt were to arise here, consider the case of a (mya ngan) mirage in a desert or wilderness where even a small object appears large.
fix.replace: Alternatively, even if that doubt could arise there, there is no such doubt in the case where, in deserts, even a small object appears large.

errors.english: those standing to the side whose eyes are not corrupted
errors.why: The observers are those standing beside the illusionists (mig 'khrul mkhan); the illusionists are dropped.

note: A sound rendering of the Pramāṇa argument on the undivided mind; the desert example loses its point.

errors.english: With mouths filled with saliva, they drink from it as if from a vessel filled with wine.
errors.why: They drink the (woman's) mouth, full of saliva, as if it were a vessel of wine; the saliva-filled mouth is what is drunk, not the drinkers'.

errors.english: This [note: existence] arises from causes
errors.why: In context 'she/that' refers to the wife (or body) just called 'mine', as the stanza's conclusion 'my wife' shows, not to existence in general.

note: Generally faithful verse translation of the meditation on the body and on 'mine'; a few loose spots.

errors.english: namely, the claim that birth and destruction cannot be otherwise
errors.why: The opponent's reason is 'because arising and destruction would otherwise (i.e. without intrinsic nature) be untenable', not that they 'cannot be otherwise'.

fix.find: namely, the claim that birth and destruction cannot be otherwise
fix.replace: namely, "because birth and destruction would otherwise be untenable"

errors.english: according to your own desire
errors.why: 'dod pa here is the opponent's tenet/assertion, not desire.

note: The Madhyamaka argument is mostly followed, but the opponent's reason is misstated.

errors.english: Regarding the phrase "because there is no result existing from that projection," the three specific aspects to be analyzed are shown to be preceded by the doubts of the (tirthikas) non-Buddhist extremists, the noble (shravakas), and the (bodhisattvas) respectively.
errors.why: The tīrthikas, śrāvakas and bodhisattvas are those to be distinguished by the three qualifications ('because there is no result' etc.) implied by it, and are presented with preceding doubts; 'existing from that projection' qualifies the three qualifications, not the quoted phrase.

note: Good rendering of the compassion/habituation argument for the Buddha as pramāṇa; the closing sentence is garbled.
Faithful rendering of the commentary on the bath-powder and spring similes for the first and second dhyāna.

errors.english: The term perfectly spread was not initially applied to these types of bedding.
errors.why: The comment is on the wording: the prefix 'properly' (yang dag par) was not prefixed to the word 'spread bedding'.

fix.find: The term perfectly spread was not initially applied to these types of bedding.
fix.replace: The word "perfectly" was not prefixed to the term "spread bedding."

errors.english: all types of bedding, such as those placed on rock and elsewhere
errors.why: Rock and the like are themselves included as 'bedding' (bases), not bedding placed on rock.

errors.english: there is no need to doubt that the procedure differs from moving it from its location
errors.why: The Tibetan says one need not suspect that the offence arises by any procedure other than removal from the place; the English implies the procedure does differ.

fix.find: there is no need to doubt that the procedure differs from moving it from its location
fix.replace: there is no need to suspect that the offence arises by a procedure other than moving it from its location

errors.english: Wherever even a single minute atom is moved, it constitutes a shift from the location.
errors.why: It is the whole object (thams cad) moving even by the measure of an atom that counts as removal from place, not the moving of a single atom of it.

fix.find: Wherever even a single minute atom is moved, it constitutes a shift from the location.
fix.replace: When the whole object moves even by the measure of a minute atom, it constitutes a shift from the location.

note: The Vinaya theft casuistry is broadly followed but several technical points about what constitutes removal are misread.

errors.english: Through realization they are made to appear mixed.
errors.why: The verse says conceptual cognition (vikalpa) mixes the unmixed own-natures; 'realization' inverts the epistemic value of the agent.

fix.find: Through realization they are made to appear mixed.

errors.english: It is appropriate to distinguish between them
errors.why: ཡང་རུང continues the alternative begun on the previous side ('either mixes ... or distinguishes'), it does not mean 'it is appropriate'.

errors.english: It is shown that the nature of the consciousness of the subject is connected to that very realization of its own essence.
errors.why: The 'own nature' is shown to be the nature of the cognition, the property-bearer (dharmin) connected with validity, while cognizing its own nature; chos can is not 'the subject'.

note: Difficult commentary on conventional validity; the argument is partly recoverable but key terms and connections are misread.

errors.english: If you claim that the "ultimate" is an object of interest for one who desires it, then it is merely a desire.
errors.why: The author concedes the first alternative: if 'ultimate' bodhicitta means aspiration taking the ultimate as object through conviction (adhimukti), that is simply accepted; the English turns the concession into a dismissal.

fix.find: If you claim that the "ultimate" is an object of interest for one who desires it, then it is merely a desire.
fix.replace: If "ultimate" means [the mind] whose nature is aspiration, taking [the ultimate] as its object through conviction (adhimukti), that is simply accepted.

errors.english: Being held as the Supreme Quality (agra-dharma) the fourth level of the Path of Preparation is like the foundation of the earth because, by being free from subject and object,
errors.why: gzung ba is the grasped object of the pair 'grasped and grasper'; the sentence says 'at the supreme-dharma stage, being free of grasped and grasper ...', not 'being held as'.

fix.find: Being held as the Supreme Quality (agra-dharma) the fourth level of the Path of Preparation is like the foundation of the earth because, by being free from subject and object,
fix.replace: At the Supreme Quality (agra-dharma) the fourth level of the Path of Preparation, it is like the depths beneath the earth because, by being free from grasped object and grasping subject,

errors.english: *Flower Ornament Sutra* (Gandavyuha Sutra) The Array of Stems Sutra
errors.why: sDong po bkod pa is the Gaṇḍavyūha; 'Flower Ornament Sutra' is the Avataṃsaka, of which it is only a part.

errors.english: to show the standard progression
errors.why: dkyus ma is the main/running text: 'to explain the text itself'.

errors.english: because it depends on the desire for a perfect body and so forth
errors.why: Perfect body etc. depend on (are at the command of) one's wish, as with the good vase; it is not the abandonment that depends on desiring them.

note: The polemic and the stage-by-stage similes are partly misconstrued; needs a careful pass on the argument and path terminology.

errors.english: appears connected with interrupting the term "non-annihilation"
errors.why: The word 'non-cessation' is said to be connected with 'non-annihilation' across intervening words (at a distance), not with 'interrupting' it.

note: Accurate sūtra dialogue and a mostly faithful account of the ordering of the eight negations.

errors.english: If one hears someone inside, one should wait.
errors.why: The rule is that when the signal is heard, the one already inside must also make a sound, as the following commentary sentence explains.

fix.find: If one hears someone inside, one should wait.
fix.replace: When this is heard, the one who has entered there should also [make a sound].

errors.english: Regarding the downfalls [note: referring to infractions of the Vinaya or monastic code]...
errors.why: ltung ba here begins the next rule about falling waste (followed by 'dig a pit'), not Vinaya offences; the note misleads.

note: Clear and usable rendering of the latrine regulations with sūtra and gloss well separated; one rule misread.
